body.flop_note: Per neuron, non-refractory path (amortized): adapt_decay mul; (v_rest-vm)*leak; +gain*acc; -w. Spike path / atomics excluded from FLOP count (control + atomics).

notes: Accounting from rse-hpc-lab/exercises/08-connectome-lif/connectome_kernels.cuh k_integrate — per-neuron lower bound on DRAM traffic.
29 bytes / 6 FLOPs ⇒ 0.2069 flop/byte. Ridge sm_120 = 42.9 flop/byte (FP32 class, measured 2026-09-14) ⇒ deeply memory-bound (correct for LIF integrate).
Spike queue atomics + hash stim are latency/control — not added to FLOP numerator on purpose.

MEASURED 2026-09-14, ncu 2025.3.1, RTX 5060 Ti (sm_120), 1 launch, F=1, n=166700, grid 288 x block 256: lts__t_bytes.sum = 4,735,680 B = 28.41 B/neuron against 29.00 counted, 0.9796x -> the byte model is CONFIRMED at L2 within 2.1%.

Same launch, dram__bytes.sum = 2,509,056 B = 15.05 B/neuron, 0.5190x. Roughly half the state never crosses the memory controller: the 9.00 MB working set at F=1 is L2-resident between steps. Reproduce: lith-probe intensity-check fixtures/intensity/k_integrate.json --ncu fixtures/ncu/k_integrate-sm_120-2026-09-14.csv --elements 166700 --ncu-level l2
known_limits: Refractory path does fewer FLOPs and still touches the same traffic — intensity is an upper bound on arithmetic density.
peak_tflops measured 2026-09-14: 15.37 TFLOP/s achieved SGEMM. DRAM 358.43 GB/s, median of 6 runs, 4.9% spread, clocks not locked.

[KNOWN LIMIT] The `dram` level on these moves is the design intent (cold, large-instance), not what this machine does at F=1 — where L2 absorbs 48% of it. `--ncu` without `--ncu-level l2` reports ABSORBED, and that is the honest reading. The DRAM lower bound is only reached once the working set exceeds L2; the instance count at which that happens is NOT MEASURED.

[KNOWN LIMIT] One launch, one problem size, clocks not locked (ncu holds base clock by default, which changes time but not byte counts). No repetition: byte counters are deterministic per launch, timing is not and none is claimed here.
